name: X-linked Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy with Deafness
aliases: X-linked Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy with Sensorineural Deafness

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked HSAN with Deafness

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Evidence of sensory neuropathy affecting pain and temperature sensation
Signs of autonomic nervous system involvement such as anhidrosis or orthostatic hypotension
X-linked inheritance pattern with affected male relatives
Identification of pathogenic variant in the causative gene (e.g., PRPS1)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (sensorineural deafness, sensory neuropathy, autonomic dysfunction) must be present; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by family history and genetic testing where available.

searchTerms: hearing loss from nerve damage both ears

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loss of pain and temperature sensation
searchTerms: loss of ability to feel pain and temperature

pathognomonic.notes: Includes impaired sweating and orthostatic hypotension
searchTerms: autonomic nervous system problems including no sweating
loss of automatic body functions with absent sweating
muscle weakness in hands or feet

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes
Gait disturbance due to sensory ataxia
searchTerms: loss of balance due to sensory problems
excess sweating in unaffected body areas
increased sweating where nerves are intact
hyperactive sweat glands in normal skin

rare.symptomName: Urinary incontinence due to autonomic neuropathy
searchTerms: loss of bladder control from nerve damage
urinary leakage due to autonomic nerve problems
vision problems from optic nerve damage
blurred or disturbed vision due to optic neuropathy

laboratory: Nerve conduction studies showing sensory neuropathy
Autonomic function tests demonstrating impaired sympathetic and parasympathetic responses
imaging: MRI may show mild atrophy of peripheral nerves
genetic: Pathogenic variants in PRPS1 gene associated with X-linked HSAN with deafness
other: Skin biopsy showing loss of small unmyelinated fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including renal and cardiac

redFlags: Early onset bilateral sensorineural deafness with neuropathy
Recurrent painless injuries and ulcers due to sensory loss
references: Orphanet: X-linked hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy with deafness (ORPHA:139583)
Dyck PJ, et al. Hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathies. Neurology. 2015.
